correctness.rationale: Tensor-product spectral projections give four exhaustive entry types. Only the double-coordinate-different type can be negative. A strictly increasing ratio proves precisely one positive sign crossing; row sum one yields the sharp norm; an independent monotone derivative equation gives its unique peak. Balanced constants come from a cubic factorization; thin-board scaling from uniform expansions of the ratio and derivative at their uniquely specified roots. Source-extracted checker rebuilt finite graph matrix exponentials independently and passed 6,465 assertions. The analytical proof, not finite trials, covers all a,b>=2.

originality.rationale: Searches for squared-Laplacian heat, rook graphs, Cartesian products, Hamming distance-two kernels, line-graph formulations and endpoint norms did not reveal a statement subsuming this exact two-factor cutoff, norm and thin-board asymptotic law. The closest general papers [1,2] give eventual-positivity characterizations, not quantitative rook-graph formulas. The published three-eigenvalue barrier [3] has insufficient hypotheses when a != b (four distinct Laplacian levels); when a=b it gives no explicit values. Existing exact complete-multipartite and Boolean-cube claims cover only intersecting special graph cases such as C4, not arbitrary K_a square K_b. Priority is provisional: absence of a search hit alone is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: No exhaustive survey of older association-scheme diffusion or matrix-exponential tables was feasible; an equivalent rook-graph computation could predate this note.
Database recall and incomplete indexing are not evidence of global uniqueness.
The balanced C4 overlap with earlier complete-multipartite and Boolean-cube results is excluded from the originality claim except as a consistency case.

value.rationale: The nonnegative-time set of this mass-preserving biharmonic smoother determines precisely when it preserves every positive input; the maximum-coordinate operator norm determines worst-case amplification. A complete two-factor rook-graph family with up to four spectral levels has a nontrivial no-gap positivity law, exact peak time, and sharp endpoint norm. Contrasting balanced and fixed-width asymptotics show that the recovery delay grows logarithmically in fast spectral units while transient norm amplification decays, a motivated quantitative structural distinction.
